subject: Unscheduled hotfix notice — tokenization regression impacting short prompts
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finify.com>, Finify Ops <ops@finify.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 02:12:00 -00:00
Subject: Unscheduled hotfix notice — tokenization regression impacting short prompts

Hi Elena / Finify Ops team,

We just detected a regression in the tokenizer layer that can truncate or mis-tokenize very short prompt inputs for a small subset of model variants (affecting ~0.4% of tokens for sequences under 12 chars). The issue appeared after yesterday's kernel update and has caused some unexpected completions for short transaction descriptors.

Immediate actions we're taking (ETA in-line):
- Rolling an emergency hotfix to the serving fleet (started now; ~15–25 minute rollout).
- Applying a short-lived routing rule to avoid the affected variant for your org while we deploy (effective in 5 minutes).
- Collecting request-level logs for impacted requests (we will provide a pulled log bundle).

Impact for Finify: possible truncated descriptors in automated reconciliation flows. We are prioritizing your account for the hotfix and routing change. No data exfiltration observed.

We will update this thread at each milestone. If you need us to pause traffic entirely while we validate, let me know and we can enact a short mitigation window.

Apologies for the interruption — I know this is sensitive for reconciliation flows.

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tokenization-failure-logs-02-14.txt (log)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finify.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 02:24:38 -05:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled hotfix notice — tokenization regression impacting short prompts

Thanks for the heads up, David.

Can you confirm whether any production reconciliations failed or were silently incorrect between 00:00–02:00 UTC? Our monitoring alerted earlier with a spike in mismatch counts. If you have a quick estimate of the percentage of outbound reconciliation jobs affected that would be helpful.

If you plan to pause traffic, please coordinate with Ops — we'll need a 10-minute heads-up.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz, Head of Platform Engineering
Finify Payments
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@finify.com>, Finify Ops <ops@finify.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 02:30:10 -00:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled hotfix notice — tokenization regression impacting short prompts

On Sat, Feb 14, 2026 at 02:24 AM Elena Ruiz <elena@finify.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether any production reconciliations failed or were silently incorrect between 00:00–02:00 UTC?

Quick update: rollout started at 02:14 UTC to 10% of ingress nodes, expanding to 100% via progressive canary over ~20 minutes. Early telemetry shows error rate on the affected model variant dropping to baseline after the first canary wave.

Preliminary impact estimate for Finify (from sampled logs): ~1.1% of reconciliation API calls during 00:45–01:30 UTC show token mismatches. We are continuing a targeted log pull to produce a definitive number and will share the bundle within 90 minutes.

If Finify prefers, we can trigger a temporary route pause for your org for the next 15 minutes while the last canary wave completes — please advise.

Marcus
Sr. Incident Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: hotfix-20260214.patch (patch)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finify.com>, Finify Ops <ops@finify.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 03:05:45 -00:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled hotfix notice — tokenization regression impacting short prompts

Elena —

Thanks for flagging. We completed the full fleet rollout at 02:40 UTC and validated across the same reconciliation flows you described. Summary so far:
- Hotfix deployed to 100% of serving nodes at 02:40 UTC.
- End-to-end tests against Finify sample data show no truncation for previously failing short prompts.
- Definitive impact: 0.98% of reconciliation API calls in the sampled window were affected; root cause traced to a kernel-level token boundary change introduced in the 20260213 build.

We have enabled a temporary routing rule for your org between 02:16–02:45 UTC; all routed traffic after 02:45 used the updated variant. I attached the log extract and the patch for your records.

Next steps (postmortem and follow-up):
- We'll publish a short postmortem in 24–48 hours with timeline and the rollback/testing guardrails.
- We're adding a targeted regression test to the CI that replays short-prompt reconciliation examples to prevent recurrence.

If you'd like a synchronous readout, we can hop on a 20-minute call today.

—Monica
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finify.com>, Finify Ops <ops@finify.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -00:00
Subject: Follow-up: hotfix confirmed — postmortem & next steps

Elena / team,

Thanks again for the quick coordination this morning and sorry for the disruption. Final notes:

- Incident resolved at 02:45 UTC after full hotfix rollout.
- Definitive customer impact (Finify): 0.98% of reconciliation calls within 00:45–01:30 UTC; no PII exposure and no downstream data loss identified.
- Permanent fixes: kernel build reverted for serving variants until additional validation is added; regression unit added to CI; canary policy tightened for tokenizer-related kernel changes.

We published an internal postmortem and a customer-facing summary here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2B_hotfix_postmortem

If you'd like, we will schedule a 30-minute review with your engineering leadership next week to walk the postmortem and confirm compensating controls.

Apologies again — we'll keep you posted on the long-form postmortem and any related SLA credit discussions (we will proactively evaluate given the customer impact).

Best,
David Kim
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
